### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx`  _(via ComponentPropsMap (symbol, a top-level const object))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ComponentPropsMap (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via ComponentPropsMap (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via ComponentPropsMap (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 16d090ede01e8e940313364603a254a659a2355b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6c3cebba4028c99a7ab83a2775eab435b50912f8` — the merge of head `60f75eeb2786e9a2235bb7c4f900bc820a85ff8d` into base `16d090ede01e8e940313364603a254a659a2355b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6c3cebba4028c99a7ab83a2775eab435b50912f8 && git checkout 6c3cebba4028c99a7ab83a2775eab435b50912f8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 16d090ede01e8e940313364603a254a659a2355b 60f75eeb2786e9a2235bb7c4f900bc820a85ff8d && git checkout -B drift-repro 16d090ede01e8e940313364603a254a659a2355b && git merge --no-ff 60f75eeb2786e9a2235bb7c4f900bc820a85ff8d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 16d090ede01e8e940313364603a254a659a2355b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 16d090ede01e8e940313364603a254a659a2355b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `076d7a79fac705d51bc9111d3af52835c9a5b5a2`

Reviewed at 2026-09-22T17:50Z by the at-tier review subagent the `domain:spec#5` seat spawned after measuring itself below tier. Inputs: the card, the seat's claim and the dev report, the PR body, the three-file diff against merge base `16d090ede0`, and objectui at the live pin `87af769e9a3ee28ace099fdd653d3ebd79fe82e2` in a fresh clone of my own (the sibling checkout sits at `0cf2d664`, a descendant of the pin). Check conclusions are the head's check-runs; no gate family was re-run locally for a verdict.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`Clause-②: no` is TRUE, proven from the patch and not from the round's word.** 362 changed lines across `ui/component.zod.ts` and `ui/component.test.ts`; every one opens with `*`, `/**`, `*/` or `//`, and both files are byte-identical to base once comments are stripped. No key, `.describe()` string, export, refusal text or accept set moves; nothing regenerates. The review is owed on the path limb and on the lane rule, not because anything in the contract changed.
- **N3, re-measured here against the pin:** `ObjectGantt.tsx:2181` is `?? resolveInlineI18nLabel(schema.label, displayLocale)`, the file's only `schema.label` read outside comments (`resolveInlineI18nLabel` is the local alias of `@objectstack/spec/ui`'s `resolveI18nLabel`, imported at `:33`, so the record's symbol name holds). `ObjectGantt.tsx:503` is `const result = GanttConfigSchema.safeParse(config);` under `if (schema.gantt)` at `:501`. The card's `:1871` is `// -- Quick-create dialog removed --` and its `:500` is a comment line. Both handover numbers CONFIRMED, both card numbers REFUTED. Whether the card's numbers held at the retired pin cannot be read from a shallow sibling; the round said so instead of pretending, and it changes nothing — the converted records assert the live pin only.
- **N4, the eleven conversions, each backed by a re-read — measured with the gate's own `--list` on the two files at base and at head:** base 29 asserting / 48 historical / 7 assertion with 30 historical naming `53ded82b`, 11 of them in the two files; head 43 / 37 / 7 with 19 naming `53ded82b`, 0 in the two files, and the 19 sit in exactly the files the report lists (`migrations/registry.ts` 4, `conversions/registry.ts` 2, `ui/view.zod.ts` 2, `ui/view.test.ts` 2, the stage-order migration 2, one each in seven more). 30 minus 11 is 19; 29 plus 11 plus the 3 gate-invisible `objectui pin` records brought into population is 43. Both reconcile.
- **Every anchor in the added lines was opened in the pinned tree and reads what the record says it reads:** ObjectMap (`:149-157`, `:168-176`, `:182-183`, `:236`, `:239`, `:289`, `:295`, `:298`, `:341`, `:377`, `:382`, `:385`, `:814-815`, `:895-896`, `:946`, `:1042-1043`, `:1058`), `record-source.ts` (`:292`, `:296`, `:303`), the registry shells (`plugin-map/src/index.tsx:68` and `:78`, `plugin-gantt/src/index.tsx:121`), ObjectGantt (`:501-503`, `:613`, `:844-845`, `:853`, `:855`, `:1333-1334`, `:1485`, `:1487`, `:1615`, `:1682`, `:1985`, `:2136`, `:2139`, `:2142-2144`, `:2179-2185`), ObjectTree (`:235-248`, `:236`, `:578-582`, `:741-753`, `:750-751`, `:775-776`, `:813-814`, `:871`, `:891`, `:908`, `:922`, `:985`), ObjectKanban (`:1210`, `:1218-1219`, `:1468`, `:1484-1497`, `:1587`), ObjectCalendar (`:921-935`, `:936`, `:938-939`, `:1218`, `:1228-1241`, `:1293`), ObjectTimeline (`:29`, `:254-256`, `:262`, `:279`, `:283`, `:325-328`, `:341-342`, `:346`, `:404-407`, `:420`, `:442`, `:444`, `:451`, `:476-479`, `:487`, `:502`, `:555-556`, `:570`, `:647`, `:650-653`, `:668`, `:706`, `:769-788`, `:772`, `:785`, `:840-841`), timeline `renderer.tsx` (`:1215`, `:1442-1457`, `:1505`) and `plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx:1725`.
- **The three deleted-read rewrites and the count are right.** `ObjectMap.tsx` `getDataConfig` is one `resolveRecordSourceConfig(schema, 'view-data')` statement at `:182-183`, with the shorthand's deletion recorded at `:150-157` (objectui#8348) and the props-channel note at `:168-176`. `ObjectTree.tsx` carries `titleField` only inside the docblock that records the rung's deletion (objectui#8841); `getTreeConfig` at `:235-248` resolves `labelField` with no `titleField` fallback. `ObjectKanban.tsx:1210` reads `schema.navigation` with no cast while `ObjectCalendar.tsx:936` still reads `(schema as any).navigation`, ledgered at `:921-935` (objectui#8651). `ElementDataSourceGate` in the registry shells: map 3, gantt 3, grid 3, calendar 3, tree 0 — the zero stands and a carried 7-each would have been wrong.
- **The reversal is RIGHT and its anchor is WRONG BY ONE — the finding.** `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx`'s `case 'tree'` arm (`:3261-3275`) still emits `labelField: treeCfg.labelField || treeCfg.titleField || 'name'`, so the prescription naming `titleField` is still true and leaving it untouched was correct. But that line is `:3270`, and the diff writes `ListView.tsx:3271` twice — in `OBJECT_TREE_FLAT_CONFIG_GUIDANCE`'s docblock in `component.zod.ts`, quoted right beside the number, and in the flat-config-keys test comment in `component.test.ts`. `:3271` is `fields: treeCfg.fields || effectiveFields,`. The file is identical at `87af769e9a3e` and at the sibling's `0cf2d664`, so this is a transcription slip on the pinned tree, not a wrong tree. It is still an asserting record, in a source file that ships, whose number does not hold at the pin it asserts, in a PR whose whole deliverable is that its numbers hold — and the gate cannot see it because the anchor carries no content assertion, which is precisely the class the card names. It goes back for a fix rather than out as a follow-up card: the last review that carried two wrong comment line numbers as non-blocking produced this card.
- **Precision nits, to fold into the same fix, none blocking on its own:** `ObjectTree.tsx:197-210` cited as the docblock that records why — the section runs `:197-218` and the third retiring measurement sits at `:215-218`; `plugin-tree/src/index.tsx:28-32` — the `tree` input object is `:27-31`; `ListView.tsx:3261-3276` — the arm closes at `:3275`; `ObjectGantt.tsx:1849` is the blank line above the dependency-delete callback's comment, so "lands in an unrelated callback" is loose rather than false.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec` with `Clause-②: no` and no direction arm: consistent. Not `minor` — nothing widens. Not `skip-changeset` — `packages/spec` `files[]` carries `src/**/*.zod.ts`, and `npm pack --dry-run` on this head lists `src/ui/component.zod.ts` and zero `src/**/*.test.ts`, so the changed comment bytes publish from a released package.

**Declared conflict 1 (changeset) — ruling: the round is right.** The os-dev role file's fast path (`.claude/agents/os-dev.md:298`) lists comments among what does not publish, but the line above it (`:297`) states the criterion that line abbreviates: published means what each package's `files[]` actually ships. For this package the abbreviation is false and the criterion governs; the tarball measurement with a positive and a negative control is the role file's own `:299` method. `skip-changeset` would have been wrong here.

**The one red check on this head is the label carrier, not the diff.** `Check Changeset` passed on the `opened` run (job 106858270135) and failed on the `labeled` run (job 106859962282) because `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` reads `needs:contract-review` as a clause-② `yes` declaration and then demands `minor`. #19675 on this same card showed the identical success, failure, success sequence around its label. It clears when the seat strips the label on a PASS record; ⛔ it is not cleared by raising the changeset to `minor`, which would declare a widening that did not happen.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Declared conflict 2 (`ASSERTED_ANCHOR_FLOOR` left at 7) — ruling: honest, and the gap is real.** The gate's header says coverage is a ratchet, not a migration, and that `--verify-anchors` prints the worklist at the one moment someone is already re-reading anchors. That moment was this round. Measured in a worktree of my own against my clone at the pin (a measurement, not the gate's verdict; CI runs the gate without objectui): worklist 197 to 204, the two files 95 to 102 (`component.zod.ts` 68 to 74, `component.test.ts` 27 to 28), 7 assertions verified, exit 0. Leaving the floor overstates nothing. But the file-surface argument is thin — the floor is one integer in the script that exists for this — and the finding in ① is exactly what one content assertion beside `ListView.tsx:3270` would have caught at write time. Recommended for the fix commit (raise the floor to 8 with that one assertion) or for a carrier; not a condition of PASS on the next head.
- **Gates.** 83 derived / 83 run / 0 not measured is the round's reconciliation; the four exit-3 families are each reported as re-run to 0 after a build, none as a pass on its exit-3 run. On the head at review time: 18 success, 1 failure (the label-carrier red above), 6 skipped, 11 in progress. Landing waits for convergence as usual.
- **Report inaccuracy, non-blocking.** The dev report says the remaining gate-invisible `objectui pin 53ded82b` citations are in files this claim does not hold. Five are inside the claimed files: `component.test.ts:2313` and `:2394`, `component.zod.ts:2703`, `:2744` and `:3333`. They are other blocks' records (object-grid, object-calendar sort) and outside the card's named scope, so leaving them is fine — but the acceptance note's carrier should name them, and two are verifiably stale at the pin: `component.zod.ts:2744` cites `ObjectGrid.tsx:1457` for `schema.sort`, which the pin reads at `:1719` and `:1740` (`:1457` is `typeof hostOnPageChange === 'function';`); `component.zod.ts:3333` cites `ObjectCalendar.tsx:431` for `schema.sort`, which the pin reads at `:648` and `:728` (`:431` is a bare `//`).
- **`190fbd01` records left historical — right outcome, slightly wrong reason.** They are not a different kind of record; they are read-point records like the converted ones. What decides it is that the card does not name them and this round did not re-read them, and the honest state for an un-re-read record is the historical spelling.
- Model identifiers: none in the title, body, five commit messages (model-free trailer pair), changeset, diff or report. Governed surfaces: none of the three paths. Closing keyword: `Part of`, correct for a card whose items land separately. `open_questions`: none declared.
- **Remedy:** one commit on this branch changing `ListView.tsx:3271` to `:3270` in both places (and the range nits if wanted), then a fresh record on the new head — a diff-of-the-fix review.
